arm_taxonomy.alternative_nonexchangeable: equal-marginal (TV(A,B)=0) but non-exchangeable within-unit joint; swap invariance is FALSE yet undetectable by the marginal statistic — the documented outside-null sensitivity limitation, never charged type-I.
arm_taxonomy.power: genuine marginal-shift alternatives; demonstrate MDE 0.35 detection under their specific families.
arm_taxonomy.type_i: swap-invariance null arms, charged type-I; two null modes: 'copy' (identical realizations) and 'law_exchangeable' (iid from one per-condition law, realizations differ but the pair is exchangeable and independent across units). Both must satisfy the CP-95 upper-bound criterion.

criterion.statement: NON-EXCHANGEABLE equal-marginal alternative (a-006): the population marginals are equal (TV(A,B) = 0 exactly) but the within-unit joint is a non-exchangeable deterministic relabeling coupling, so swap invariance is FALSE. Because the marginal TV statistic is identically zero, the frozen rule cannot reject (power ~ 0). This DOCUMENTS the design's outside-null sensitivity limitation — TV=0 is never evidence that swap invariance holds — and is NEVER charged against type-I.

criterion.detail: swap-invariance null, LAW-EXCHANGEABLE mode (a-006): A/B/C are drawn iid from the SAME per-condition law, so the realizations differ unit by unit while the pair (A_i, B_i) is exchangeable and independent across units — a genuine swap-invariance null case, verified by law pre-analysis (equal per-condition distributions + iid independent generation). The within-pair permutation reference is valid, and on this discrete 4-action / n=48 design the test is empirically CONSERVATIVE; the exact CP-95 UPPER bound must still fall at or below alpha, resolved at the frozen high trial count reported in ci_method.type_i_high_trials.

sham-gate residual LEAKAGE context (reported with CI, not a frozen fitness criterion): the clause-2 warrant is granted on the OBSERVED pack, so no finite-sample rule can bound the unobserved generating process — in a small fraction of trials a contaminated-at-margin sham looks null with its warrant intact and a decisive A/B rejection promotes as the frozen rule directs. The frozen fitness criteria of this design are exactly type_i_criterion and power_target; the ABSOLUTE observation-level guarantees are pinned deterministically in the test suite (the reproduced boundary pack TV(A,C) = q_AC = margin is inconclusive, never positive; every emitted positive carries the sham warrant).

criterion.detail: swap-invariance null, COPY mode (a-006): one draw per unit is copied across A/B/C exactly (verified concordant unit-by-unit pre-analysis), so every matched pair is byte-identical and the structural rejection rate is ZERO; the CP-95 upper bound holds mechanically. sharp_h0_shared_latent additionally breaks across-unit independence (dependence-robustness) and must still control type-I.

ci_method.math: copy-mode type-I arms are structural zeros, resolved exactly at T=400 (CP-95 upper ~0.0092 at k=0). Law-exchangeable type-I arms carry a small non-zero rate and run at T=3000 (>= the 2000 floor) for a tight bound: the concentrated arm sits at a genuine, conservative ~0.039 discreteness level, and at T=3000 its CP-95 upper bound is ~0.046 < alpha=0.05 with margin, whereas T=2000 leaves only p-hat<=0.040 headroom. For power, at T=400 and p-hat=0.85 the CP lower bound is ~0.812, so the frozen target 0.8 is resolvable against true power ~0.85 or better.

thresholds.type_i_criterion: CP-95 upper bound of the swap-invariance-null rejection rate <= alpha (finite-sample type-I control under the within-pair exchangeability reference; equal-marginal arms that are jointly exchangeable are charged as type-I, non-exchangeable equal-marginal couplings are alternatives)

mde_selection.method: smallest grid effect whose measured power CP-95 LOWER bound >= power_target, at the exact frozen procedure (n = 48 units per condition, 10000-iteration within-pair permutation null, sham axis holding the null)

null_statement: Operative confirmatory null (within-unit joint swap invariance): for every matched experimental unit i, the joint distribution of the paired terminal outcomes is invariant under exchanging presentation labels A and B — (Y_iA, Y_iB) =d (Y_iB, Y_iA) — subject to the preregistered across-unit independence / exchangeability-block assumptions. This implies equality of the population-marginal terminal-action distributions, but the within-pair permutation test is NOT claimed to be an exact test of bare population-marginal equality alone.
schedule_verification: every trial's generated potential-outcome schedule is verified unit-by-unit against its arm's declared null status AND null_mode BEFORE analysis, with a mode-specific proof that is never weakened: a copy-mode null axis is proven by IDENTICAL REALIZATION (A_i == B_i == C_i at every matched unit, so the pair is byte-identical); a law-exchangeable null axis is proven by LAW (equal per-condition distributions + iid independent generation, the generating law is swap-invariant though realizations differ); an alternative axis is proven by REALIZATION DISCORDANCE. A completed arm is itself the proof — verification raises before any statistic otherwise.
